title: Phoenix Lights boomerang over the hospice workers
summary: James Fox tells of Phoenix Lights boomerang over the hospice workers, about March 13, 1997 at Arizona, and says they saw it or took part. As told, not a fact.

tellings.difference: This telling adds that there were five witnesses, that the craft took about five minutes to pass overhead because of its size, and that they did nothing while it passed. It gives no date, place or boomerang shape.
tellings.link_reason: Both have James Fox recounting a group of witnesses he interviewed who watched a huge craft pass slowly overhead. That matches his account of the hospice workers who saw the Phoenix Lights boomerang. The telling gives no place or date, so this match is inferred from the matching details and is not certain.

as_told.title: Five witnesses watch a huge craft pass overhead for five minutes and do nothing

plain: A documentary filmmaker, James Fox, says that in the 1990s he interviewed hospice workers who saw a huge boomerang-shaped craft over Arizona on March 13, 1997, the night of the mass sighting known as the Phoenix Lights. According to Fox, five of them sat looking up as it passed overhead, and it was so big it took about five minutes to go by. He ties the case to Arizona's governor at the time, Fife Symington, and tells it because it would mean an enormous unknown craft flew over a city in plain view.
